evaluation: Object lifetime and manual garbage collection across the accepted optimized R pipeline
decision: Keep only the filtering cleanup. Other tested candidates did not demonstrate meaningful process peak-memory savings.
implementation_language: All candidates are R only, without new dependencies or non-R scientific code. Python/shell controls measure and validate experiments only.

filtering_adopted.design: Two complete AB/BA pairs per filtering mode; exact outputs and terminal guards passed. Applicable edge cases are recorded in the linked benchmark.

extraction_rejected.recommendation: Do not incorporate extraction rm changes: insignificant peakRSS reduction and increased CPU.
extraction_rejected.scientific_validation: Both AB/BA pairs exact with zero exemptions and no numerical review.
extraction_rejected.scope: One large real LIB2 chunk41; no extrapolated claim about all task sizes.
extraction_rejected.memory: Worker process peakRSS. SLURM batchRSS includes subsequent comparison and is not the worker performance metric.

vcf_forced_gc_rejected.validation: Both entire GRanges objects identical in values/types/attributes/order;68 edge comparisons passed; source/input/environment terminal guards passed.
vcf_forced_gc_rejected.limitation: The68-case suite includes consistent failure parity for truly empty VCF records; not a success claim for every format.
vcf_forced_gc_rejected.reason: Mean process peak rises11.76% (~1.89GiB) despite1.07% lower CPU. ManualGC timing does not guarantee lower peak.

vcf_release_only_rejected.decision: Reject early-release-only VCF candidate: no meaningful peak-memory improvement.
vcf_release_only_rejected.validation: Complete GRanges identical in data, type, attributes and order; 68 fixture comparisons passed; worker and validation terminal source/input/environment guards passed.
vcf_release_only_rejected.limitation: One same-node AB diagnostic. 68-case suite includes consistent error parity for truly empty-record VCF inputs, not universal support. CPU reduction is descriptive; peak change is negligible. This does not justify more repetitions or production changes.
vcf_release_only_rejected.scope: Release raw vcfR object after eager field extraction without added forced GC. Complete worker CPU includes waited descendants; peak is largest-process RSS, not concurrent allocation memory.

final_output_rejected.decision: Reject output export-slot cleanup: no meaningful performance gain despite exact complete outputs
final_output_rejected.reason: No meaningful reduction in complete operation peak (~35.23GiB both). User wants measured significant memory wins; no repeat needed to adopt an ineffectual cleanup.
final_output_rejected.scope: One complete same-node baseline-first pair including worker/ordinary assembly/export/cleanup and waited descendants; single-process high-water, not allocation or simultaneous process-tree peak.

burden_rejected.evaluation: Native R burden object-lifetime cleanup and explicit GC
burden_rejected.scientific_implementation: R only; accepted375 coverage, annotation, joins and ordinary QS contract retained; no DuckDB or hybrid code in either arm
changes: Release sensitivity query ranges after the last input, followed by conditional GC.
Release BED scratch vectors before the existing GC; release all-zero block scratch before continuing.
Collect after the nested sensitivity variant tables are actually removed from the sensitivity list column.

workload.scope: Complete burden task with the first15 of the pinned ordered60 real filtered inputs
workload.public_output: One ordinary result.qs2 plus the existing eight BED/index exports
workload.worker_boundary: Includes R startup/loading, input I/O, coverage and annotation, calls, sensitivity, ordinary QS serialization and BED/index writes. Environment preflight and validation are separately accounted.

comparison_limitations: The native15 comparator is a reused, byte-verified earlier run on cl017; the GC candidate ran on cl015, with additional phase probes. Same scientific inputs/config/SIF do not make their resource timing a matched experiment.

The unchanged prefix through input15 already used291.070 fewer CPU seconds in the candidate run before the first added cleanup; unchanged annotation also ran faster. The observed total15.46% CPU reduction cannot be assigned to GC.

The approximately20.85GiB process HWM was incurred before input loading. Identical RSS before/after GC does not prove no heap space became reusable, but no material peak-memory improvement was demonstrated.

exact_validation.fixture_result: All R sources parse; lifetime-stripped AST exact;24 actual BED-writer edge fixtures exact
exact_validation.comparison: R identical per named scientific component; ordered decompressed BED payload equality;16 own-index rebuild proofs and matching indexed query outputs; no tolerances or NA/NaN normalization

burden_rejected.accounting: Process max_rss_kib is the largest process high-water mark. Cgroup and SLURM batch memory include a different scope and file cache; their values are retained in the full receipts and are not labeled R heap.
burden_rejected.conclusion: Do not adopt these three burden cleanup changes and do not launch a matched repeat or full60 GC trial from this screen: no material process peak reduction or direct cleanup RSS reduction was observed. Scientific exactness passed.
burden_rejected.separate_scale_observation: A future unchanged native60 phase trace from the independent hybrid study can locate its peak relative to cleanup boundaries. This is separate from the closed GC evaluation, does not test GC efficacy, and does not imply a memory bound from object.size.

other_scripts_reviewed.finding: Summaries remain required output; transient objects are scoped in per-chromosome functions. No further large clearly dead named object was identified that merits another GC-only benchmark now.
Prepared intervals are retained output and saved immediately; no extra large dead object between high-memory phases identified.
Large work is done in called package/external build operations; top-level named objects are paths/configuration. No justified extra top-level rm/GC insertion identified.
Accumulated variant list is required for final output. Main candidate is shared load_vcf lifetime tested above; no separate cosmetic collections added.
Products are streamed/copied/checksummed rather than retained as complete R data; no substantial scientific object-lifetime candidate identified.

limits: CPU is actual user plus system time including waited descendants. Validation and setup controls are separate; no new whole-pipeline performance total is inferred.
Process peak RSS is not R heap, aggregate simultaneous workflow memory, cgroup/file-cache memory or a minimum safe allocation.

A cleanup can make heap space reusable without decreasing RSS, and cannot lower a peak already reached. No significant memory benefit was measured for the rejected candidates on their tested workloads.

The burden screen used 15 of 60 ordered real inputs and a reused native comparator on a different node. Its observed faster CPU is not attributed to GC; a larger-input memory bound is not established.

Existing manual GC remains. Rejected candidate implementations and test controls stay outside production; public QS2 schemas, exports, deterministic ordering and Nextflow publication rules are unchanged.

The independent R-coverage/DuckDB-call hybrid study remains frozen. No changes from this separate GC screen were inserted or tested in that prototype; its existing restoration/close collection remains included. Any adoption requires a separate user decision.
